points.description: States that infinite recursion can be caused by the recursion step being defined incorrectly (the recursive case is wrong, so the function does not reduce towards the base case). Equivalent wording earns the marks.
States that infinite recursion can be caused by the base case not being included (or omitted) in the definition, so the recursion never stops. Equivalent wording earns the marks.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for naming both causes: an incorrectly defined recursion step and a missing base case, each worth 2.5. Each cause is a separate, all-or-nothing idea, so a student who names only one cause earns 2.5. Answers that name neither cause, or name only unrelated causes such as syntax errors, earn no marks. Any equivalent wording of the two ideas is accepted.
